metaDescription: Lost power, a tripped breaker, or a burning smell in South Florida? Ghost Crown Electric finds the fault and restores power day or night. Licensed and local.
h1: 24/7 Emergency Electrical and Power Restoration in South Florida
intro: Eleven at night, the AC is dead, and the breaker will not stay on. That is the call this company was built around. Our licensed crew traces the fault, makes it safe, and restores power. After-hours visits carry a premium we name before we roll.

definition.heading: What emergency electrical and power restoration cover
definition.body: Failures that cannot wait: a dead circuit, a panel that will not reset, a burning smell, sparking, or a sudden loss of power. We diagnose first and price the fix second, so you know the number before work begins.

symptoms.title: Part of the building lost power
symptoms.body: One unit, one wing, or one circuit is dark while the rest works. When the outage stops at your property line, it is a fault we can locate and repair.

symptoms.title: A breaker will not stay on
symptoms.body: It trips again in seconds, or will not reset at all. That circuit is overloaded, shorted, or failing, and it needs a licensed eye, not a bigger breaker.

symptoms.title: Burning smell or scorch marks
symptoms.body: Heat where there should be none. Stop using that circuit and call. This is exactly the kind of sign we come out for.

symptoms.title: Half the property is dark
symptoms.body: Half the building works and large appliances act strange. That usually means a lost leg of incoming power, a serious fault at the service.

process.title: You call and we triage
process.body: What failed, what still works, and whether the neighbors have power. That separates a utility outage from a fault on your side.

process.title: On-site diagnosis
process.body: We find the actual fault with meters and method, not guesswork.

process.title: One forecast-based price
process.body: One number for the repair before we touch it, and it does not move mid-job.

process.title: Our in-house crew does the work
process.body: The crew that shows up does the repair and pulls any permit under our own license.

benefits.title: The fault is actually found
benefits.body: We repair the actual point of failure, so the power that comes back stays back.

benefits.title: A licensed electrician who answers
benefits.body: A Florida Certified Electrical Contractor and Tri-County Master Electrician, not an answering service.

benefits.title: Honest about what is ours to fix
benefits.body: If the whole neighborhood is dark, that is the utility, and we will say so rather than bill you for it.

benefits.title: One price that holds
benefits.body: One number before the repair starts, and it does not creep upward.

localSections.heading: Aging housing stock and tired panels
localSections.body: Much of South Florida was wired in the sixties, seventies, and eighties, and many of those panels are still in service. After decades of summers down here, that equipment gives out as a breaker that will not reset, a warm cover, or a lost leg.

localSections.heading: Heat, humidity, and salt air
localSections.body: Air conditioning runs eight or nine months a year, so cooling circuits carry heavy load. Salt air corrodes lugs, bus bars, and meter equipment. Corrosion adds resistance, resistance makes heat, and heat turns a slow problem into a sudden outage at night.

guide.title: The complete guide to emergency electrical and power restoration in South Florida

sections.heading: What counts as an emergency, and whose problem it is
sections.body: A true emergency is anything unsafe, like burning smells, smoke, sparking, or a problem near water, or a loss of critical power such as air conditioning in July. It comes down to where the darkness stops. Whole street dark is the utility. Stops at your property, and the fault is on your side of the meter.

sections.heading: How troubleshooting and fault location work
sections.body: Restoring power is not guesswork. We start at the source with meters, checking the service, panel, and circuit to find where power stops. Most buildings receive two legs of power, so when one is lost, usually at the meter or service, half the circuits die while the rest run.

sections.heading: When a restoration turns into a bigger fix
sections.body: Getting power back is the first job. Sometimes we restore it and find worn out equipment behind it, where the real fix is a panel upgrade or a service rebuild. We never use the moment to push it. That work gets its own visit in daylight.

faqs.question: Do you really answer the phone at night?
faqs.answer: Yes, day or night. We ask what failed and what still works, then decide with you whether a truck rolls now or whether it is safe to wait until morning and skip the after-hours premium.

faqs.question: Is my outage the power company's problem or an electrician's?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the darkness stops. Whole neighborhood out is the utility. If it stops at your property, or it is one unit while neighbors have lights, the fault is on your side of the meter and it is our lane.

faqs.question: Why did half my property lose power?
faqs.answer: Most buildings receive two legs of incoming power. When one is lost, usually at the meter or service, about half your circuits go dead while the rest keep working. That is a real fault, not a breaker you can reset.

faqs.question: Can you get the power back on the same night?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. A failed breaker or a burned connection is usually made safe and restored on the first visit. If it needs a part, a utility disconnect, or a permit, we stabilize what is safe and lay out the plan for the rest.
